# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 7 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 7 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_007_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 2, Chapter 3

**1** The tower was being built by six young men who had come with her. Many thousands of other men were bringing stones — some from the deep sea, others from the dry land — and handing them to the six young men, who received them and built with them. **2** All the stones dragged up from the deep were placed into the building just as they were, for they were smooth and fitted precisely at the joints. They locked together with one another so tightly that their seams could not be detected, and the whole tower looked as though it had been built from a single stone. **3** But the stones brought from the dry land — some of these they discarded, others they placed into the building, others they broke apart and threw far from the tower. **4** Many other stones were lying around the tower that were not used. Some were thrown far from the tower; others had cracks; others were white and round and could not fit into the building. **5** I saw other stones being hurled far away, and when they landed they rolled off the road onto trackless ground. Others fell into fire and burned there. Others landed near the water but could not roll into it, though they strained to do so. **6** When she had shown me all this she wanted to hurry away. I said, "Lady, what use is it to me to see these things if I don't know what they mean?" She turned back and said to me, "You are quite the impertinent one, wanting to know about the tower." "Yes, but please — tell me, lady." **7** "This tower," she said, "is the Church." "And who are the six young men building it?" "They are the holy angels of God who were created first of all, to whom the Lord entrusted his whole creation — to build it up, increase it, and rule over it. Through them, then, the building of the tower will be completed." **8** "And the many other men bringing stones — who are they?" "These too are holy angels of God, but the six are over them. The tower's building will be completed, and all will rejoice together around the tower and give glory to God, because the tower is finished." **9** "Lady, I would like to understand the stones," I said. "The bright, square ones that fit together — who do they represent?" She replied, "They are the apostles and bishops and teachers and deacons who walked in the holiness of God and served him with purity and reverence as bishops and teachers and deacons. Some of these have already fallen asleep; others are still living. They were always in agreement with one another and lived in peace with one another, so they heard one another. **10** That is why their joints fit together in the building of the tower." "And those dragged from the deep sea?" "These are those who have suffered for the sake of the Lord's name." **11** "And those from dry land?" "These are those who did not suffer, but whose holy way of life pleased God, as they walked in the Lord's commandments." "And those being rejected — who are they?" **12** "Those who have sinned and wish to repent; that is why they have not been thrown far from the tower — they can still be useful in the building if they repent. If they repent now, while the tower is still under construction, they will be strong in faith. But once the tower is completed there will be no more room for repentance — they will be cast aside." **13** "And the rejected, cracked ones?" "These are the sons of wickedness who have believed hypocritically and whose evil has not departed from them. They have no salvation, for their wickedness makes them unfit for the building." **14** "And those white round ones that do not fit?" "How long will you be slow to understand?" she said. "These are those who have faith but also possess the wealth of this age. When tribulation comes, they deny their Lord on account of their riches and their business dealings." "When will they become useful for the building, then?" "When," she answered, "their wealth is stripped away — the wealth that is bewitching them — they will be useful to God. For just as a round stone cannot become square unless something is cut from it, so those who are wealthy in this age cannot be useful to the Lord unless their wealth is cut away. **15** Learn this first from your own experience: when you were wealthy you were useless, but now you are useful and profitable for life. Be useful to God, for you yourself have been cut from this stone."

---

*LOGOS note: "fallen asleep" for kekoimemenoi — standard early Christian euphemism for death (1 Thess 4:13). "Sons of wickedness" = sons of iniquity, Semitic expression.*
